D-DISSOLUTION-2013_2015: Three evidence items are dissolution failures initiated between 2013 and 2015. Astellas Pharma US recalled Tarceva erlotinib tablets in September 2014 after the product failed the dissolution acceptance criteria at 24-month routine stability testing, Class II [E3]. Caraco Pharmaceutical Laboratories recalled venlafaxine hydrochloride extended-release tablets twice, in March 2014 [E8] and June 2014 [E9], in both cases after stability results showed the product did not meet drug release dissolution specifications, Class II. The remaining evidence items are dissolution or stability failures outside that window [E1][E2][E4][E5][E6][E7][E10].
D-MICROBIAL_NONSTERILE-2013_2015: Three evidence items are microbial contamination of non-sterile products initiated between 2013 and 2015. Tropichem Research Labs recalled Entertainer's Secret Throat Relief in December 2014 after microbial assay reported unacceptably high plate counts and a positive result for E. coli, Class II [E1]. Fusion Pharmaceuticals recalled the Dicopanol FusePaq Kit in May 2013 for total yeast and mould counts above USP limits, Class II [E3]. Tower Pharmacy and Compounding recalled Phenylephrine Nasal 1% Spray in November 2013 for possible microbial contamination, Class II [E5]. Vi-Jon recalled an alcohol-free antiseptic mouth rinse contaminated with Burkholderia contaminans in July 2013, Class III [E6]. The remaining items fall outside the window [E2][E4][E7][E8][E9][E10].
D-STABILITY_EXPIRY-2022_2026: Two evidence items are stability or expiry failures initiated between 2022 and 2026. Private Label Partners recalled Selenium Sulfide 2.25% Shampoo in December 2023, cited as CGMP deviations because stability data did not support the expiry date, Class II [E7]. HTO Nevada dba Kirkman recalled lidocaine sprays and creams in February 2026 because stability data did not support the expiry date, Class II [E8]. The remaining evidence items concern the same failure mode but were initiated before 2022 [E1][E2][E3][E4][E5][E6][E9][E10].
